# A window beat can show an empty black vessel with nothing inside

## Context

Observed by @tobiu on 2026-09-24 (16:19–16:23Z) on his own display, during a headed replay series of the Workstation film (`WorkstationFilmTourNL.spec.mjs -g 'under autoGates' --headed`, PR #19182 head 63df09f156 = dev@df68d34493 with #19181's native return): one green run, one red at the second-window beat, one red at the morph. The operator escalated the sighting; this ticket promotes the defect-note (Memory Core `b5912c84ec357a47`).

## The Problem

**Observation:** one drag produced a popup with a black background and nothing else in it — no pane, no tab strip.

**Series facts (from the runs' popup probe):** every created vessel closed again in all three runs (3/3, 2/2, 3/3), so the black vessel was transient, not an orphan; the first run created only two vessels because the tour stopped at its failed conversion. Which beat produced the black vessel and for how long it stayed black is unmeasured — the probe records created / loaded / closed, not what a vessel painted.

**Inference — three candidates, none proven:**
1. a born vessel painted before its document and pane materialised (the tear-out's mid-gesture birth, or the morph's birth under its 1500 ms hold);
2. the morph's retiring vessel painted after its pane had left (the re-entry cancels the tear-out, the vessel retires);
3. a vessel whose theme background never applied, so the body fell to a dark default (the class of `VesselPlaceholder`'s own history: an unaddressed component inherits the user-agent ground).

## The Architectural Reality

- Vessel birth and retirement: `src/dashboard/dock/window/TearOut.mjs` (the vessel is born mid-gesture, `birthHold` in the film's morph, `previewNodeId`), `VesselPark.mjs`, `VesselConversion.mjs`; the popup boots its own Workstation app from the `?popout=` / `?tearout=` URL and adopts the opener's theme at birth (`#18672`: an adopted instance takes its container's theme).
- The film's window beats: `GestureDriver#executeTearOutStep` (tear-out; the morph = tear-out + re-entry), `executeCrossWindowDockStep` (the second window), `NativeGestureDriver#executeNativeReturnStep` (the stack's return; the vessel closes after the transfer).

## The Fix

Measured 2026-09-25 (comments below): the black window is the **morph's vessel** (beat 16) — born, viewport mounted, and never given its pane for its whole 2.7 s life, 4 of 4 headed runs. The tear-out vessel's own first-paint void is 150–170 ms (a flash, not this sighting). Mechanism: after the whole-stack native return brings Metrics home, the item's vessel-ownership record stays in the native lifecycle registry with its window nulled; the morph's new vessel binds into that stale record, the connect handler reads it as an already-adopted (terminal-first) vessel, registers the target and skips the connect-first stage.

1. **Clear the returned items' ownership when the return's vessel retires** — the native return must leave the registry the way the DOM-grip return does, so the next tear-out of the same item starts clean and stages its pane on connect.
2. **Red-first unit arm** on the return path: after the release, `getOwner` for the returned item is null and a following connect stages.
3. **The film's morph vessel mounts its pane headed**, read by the per-frame sampler.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC-1 The instrumented headed series names the beat, the vessel and the duration of the black frame (or records five runs without one, which closes this as not reproduced with the receipt attached). *Met 2026-09-25: the morph's vessel, beat 16, empty for 2.7 s, 4 of 4 at `dev@79f81045b3` (issuecomment-5830853813); the mechanism trail in issuecomment-5830993522.*
- [ ] AC-2 After the fix the morph's vessel mounts its pane: the per-frame sampler reads pane content within 300 ms of the window's creation, headed 3 of 3 on the film-stage display; the tear-out vessel's first-paint void stays at or under 200 ms. *(Restated 2026-09-25: the earlier "and the tab strip before the re-entry" clause is dropped — the connect-first stage embodies the live pane without the document projection, so a pre-terminal vessel carries the pane and no strip by design, exactly as the tear-out vessel does for its first half second; a strip during the morph is a screenplay question, not this defect.)*
- [ ] AC-3 The film replay is green headed 3/3 at the PR head on the film-stage display, and a red-first unit arm shows the returned item's ownership cleared after the vessel's release and the next connect staging the pane.
- [ ] AC-4 The PR body names the mechanism.

## Out of Scope

The stand-in mask in the parked vessel and the merged vessel's tab-strip gap (their own tickets, filed alongside); the film's screenplay and pacing.

### @neo-fable - 2026-09-25T10:09:57Z

**Per-frame headless baseline at `dev@79f81045b3`, 2 of 2 runs (Mnemosyne, taking the ticket per the operator's 2026-09-25 steer).** A rAF sampler installed in every window through the context (emits on change) instead of a 100 ms poll, so the frame Ada's probe caught once resolves into phases. Milliseconds after the platform created the window:

| phase | tear-out vessel (`?popout=metrics`) | conversion vessel (`?popout=commits`) |
|---|---|---|
| first sampled frame, body background still `rgba(0,0,0,0)` | 44 | 27 |
| themed ground `rgb(14, 15, 13)`, nothing mounted | 127 | 94 |
| `.neo-viewport` mounted and the pane's own text present ("LIVE METRICS 99.9 System Metrics …" / "CHANGE STREAM +42 Commit Stream …") | 181 | 144 |
| tab strip (`.neo-tab-header-toolbar`) | 700 | never — the stand-in mask replaces the pane at 861 (#19186's park), closed at 4088 |

So headless the window is *nothing* for about 180 ms: the first 90–130 ms unthemed (the `color-scheme: dark` meta in `index.html` makes that canvas dark, which is why it reads as black), then the theme ground without a mount. That matches the pop-out host's design (`ViewportController`: `?popout=<id>` boots an EMPTY host; the owner's adoption mounts the vessel) — the gap is boot-to-adoption. The pane content arrives half a second before its tab chrome; that second span is a chrome-less pane, not an empty window.

Headed is unmeasured still: real window creation and the first compositor frame stretch both spans, and the sighting was headed. The same instrument runs headed on the film-stage display once the operator names a quiet window (the external display is his working screen today). Candidate fixes wait for that reading: a first-paint stand-in in the pop-out host (the themed ground plus the item's title chrome, replaced by the real projection) would cover the first span at any duration; the second span is the owner's projection order.

### @neo-fable - 2026-09-25T10:25:07Z

**Headed at `dev@79f81045b3`, 4 of 4 runs on the film-stage display (10:14–10:18Z): the black empty window is the morph's vessel, and it is empty for its whole life.** Milliseconds after the platform created each window, the range over four runs:

| window | themed ground | viewport | pane content | tab strip | closed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tear-out vessel (`metrics`, beat 3) | 98–113 | 148–172 | 148–172 (the pane's text mounts with the viewport) | 661–726 | ≈ 12.6 s, at the native return |
| conversion vessel (`commits`, beat 7) | 94–163 | 145–178 | 145–178 | never — the stand-in mask from 781–822 to its close at ≈ 4.0 s | ≈ 4.0 s |
| **the morph's vessel** (`metrics`, beat 16, born mid-gesture and retired on re-entry) | 130–160 | 163–175 | **never** | never | **2.7 s** |

So the tear-out's void is 150–170 ms headed, the same as headless, and reads as a flash. The morph births a vessel that mounts its viewport and then holds a themed, empty window for 2.7 s until the re-entry retires it: `textContent` stayed at the loader's 8 characters, no pane, no strip, in every run. That is the operator's sighting.

The contract disagrees with it: `VesselEmbodiment`'s own summary says the staged pane keeps a vessel from "becoming a black void", and the tear-out gets that stage on connect (`afterTearOutWindowConnect` → `tearOutEmbodiment.stage`) within 170 ms. The morph's vessel never does. First read: whether the connect-side stage runs for the session's second `metrics` vessel at all — same item id and window name, the first generation retired at the native return — since the stage abandons itself when the connection it began for is no longer current. The morph arm of the five-beat witness reproduces this headless with the same sampler; next on this ticket.

### @neo-fable - 2026-09-25T10:35:51Z

**Mechanism, from a headed run with the stage record, the vessel connection and the item's ownership record polled at 100 ms through the whole film (`dev@79f81045b3`, film-stage display):**

| beat | `tearOutEmbodiment.isStaged('metrics')` | connection | owner record for `metrics` |
|---|---|---|---|
| tear-out born (beat 4) | **true** | the vessel's window | — |
| tear-out committed | false (promoted) | — | the vessel's window |
| after the native return (beats 9–11) | false | — | **kept**: `{generation 1, windowId: null, windowName 'tearout-metrics', workspaceKey 'workstation-vessel:metrics'}` |
| the morph's vessel connects (beat 16) | **false — never true** | — | the **new** vessel's window id lands in that same record |
| after the re-entry | false | — | `{generation 2, windowId: null, …}` |

In isolation (headless, a fresh session) the morph stages its pane in 132–143 ms and the record clears on re-entry, first and second generation alike — so the morph path is sound. In the film it runs after a committed tear-out whose stack came home, and the whole-stack return leaves the item's vessel-ownership record in place: the native lifecycle registry keeps an owner through a release the host retains (`onRelease` → `unbind` answers `false` for a popup workspace with a host, so `released` → `onBindingReleased` → `onPaneAdopted(itemId, null)` never runs) and only nulls its window. The morph's new vessel then binds into the stale record (`onBind`: an owned item records no connection and binds as `owned`), `afterTearOutWindowConnect` reads `getOwner(…).windowId === windowId` as a terminal-first adoption, registers the target and returns without the connect-first stage — the pane never enters, and the viewer gets a themed, empty window for the born hold plus the walk back: 2.7 s.

**Reproduced headless, both grips (correction to my first draft of this comment, which named #19181 alone):** tear-out → A+B compose → the DOM-grip stack return (`executeStackReturnStep`, applied) → morph: the owner record for `metrics` reads `{generation 1, windowId: null, …}` after the return, the morph's vessel binds into it, and that vessel never mounts its pane (2.57 s, `textContent` at the loader's 8 characters). So the class is the whole-stack return home (the DOM grip since #18674 / #18684, the native frame since #19170 / #19181), and the black window is its symptom on the next tear-out of a returned item.

Fix under this ticket: when a transfer home empties a vessel and the vessel retires, clear the returned items' vessel ownership so the next tear-out starts clean and stages on connect; red-first unit arm on that path, a headless e2e arm for the morph after a return, and the film's morph vessel mounting its pane headed as the witness. ACs restated in the body.
